name: HubSpot
oneLiner: Unlisted marketplace apps are capped at 25 installs.

review.what: HubSpot Marketplace listing review (needed only to lift the 25-install cap)
review.wait: Initial review within 10 business days; full process up to 60 days from first feedback

cost.text: $0; no listing fee is stated in the listing requirements

limits.text: Before listing: a marketplace-distribution app is limited to 25 installs, excluding developer test accounts.
The 25-install cap applies to apps created or migrated on the Developer Platform from September 22, 2025.
Private-distribution apps can only be installed in up to 10 allowlisted accounts.
Before review, installers see an unverified-app warning and must type "I accept the risk" to connect.

requirements.text: New apps are created with the HubSpot CLI (v7.6.0) via `hs project create`, with redirect URLs and scopes in app-hsmeta.json.
Production redirect URLs must use HTTPS.
Listing needs at least three active installs in unaffiliated production accounts with activity in the past 30 days.
Listing needs live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs, a support contact, and a public setup guide.
Listed apps must use OAuth as the only auth method and request only the scopes they need.
Listed AI connectors must require user-level permissions or be built with HubSpot's MCP Server.

gotchas.text: Access tokens currently expire after 30 minutes, so the refresh flow must work.
You can submit only one app for listing at a time; extra submissions are rejected automatically.
Composio's managed HubSpot app is still awaiting HubSpot approval, so users see a warning; your own app avoids that once listed.
Composio's managed app cannot add scopes; a different scope set needs your own app.

steps.t: Install the HubSpot CLI, run `hs account auth`, then `hs project create` with OAuth auth and marketplace distribution
Add Composio's redirect URI and your scopes to app-hsmeta.json, then `hs project upload`
Open the app's Auth tab and copy the client ID and secret
Create a custom HubSpot auth config in Composio with the client ID, secret and scopes
Draft the privacy policy, terms and HubSpot setup guide needed for listing
Get three active unaffiliated installs, then submit the Marketplace listing for review

callbackNote: Add the redirect URI shown in Composio's dashboard (Composio's HubSpot guide uses https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) to config.auth.redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json.

sources.t: HubSpot changelog: marketplace distribution install limits
HubSpot: manage apps (distribution, install limits, warnings)

unverified: Refresh token lifetime is not stated in the OAuth quickstart.
Whether installs beyond 25 on migrated legacy apps keep working was not confirmed in fetched docs.

name: Salesforce
oneLiner: New Connected Apps are restricted; use External Client Apps.

review.what: AgentExchange (formerly AppExchange) security review, needed only to list publicly
review.wait: 1-2 weeks verification plus 3-4 weeks first test; resubmissions 2-3 weeks

cost.text: Security review fee for paid apps; no fee if you distribute for free (amount not on current docs page)

limits.text: Without passing security review you can't list on AgentExchange or distribute your solution there.
A customer org admin may need to install or approve your app before users can connect.

requirements.text: Creating Connected Apps is restricted as of Spring '26; Salesforce recommends External Client Apps instead.
Creating a Connected App now needs Salesforce Support to enable an org permission, once per org.
Security review requires ISV Partner Program enrollment, a Lightning Ready solution and a Partner Console provider profile.
API-only submissions need a Developer Edition org, false-positive notes if any, and solution documentation.
Reviewers test external web apps and services your solution uses, following where Salesforce data goes.

gotchas.text: OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC or 'app must be installed into org' means an org admin must approve or install the app.
Distributing an External Client App to other orgs is done through a second-generation managed package.
OAuth consumer credentials are global settings that must stay in a long-lived org, not in the package.
Refresh token expiry is set by the app's OAuth policy, so check it before going live.
Apps that skip pre-testing rarely pass review, and each resubmission adds 2-3 weeks.

steps.t: In Setup, search External Client Apps and create a new External Client App
Enable OAuth, add Composio's callback URL and the api, refresh_token and id scopes
Copy the consumer key and secret from the app's OAuth settings
Create a custom Salesforce auth config in Composio with the key and secret
Have each customer org's admin install or approve the app
Optional: join the ISV Partner Program and submit for AgentExchange security review

portal: Salesforce Setup > External Client Apps (in your org)
callbackNote: Add the redirect URI shown in Composio's dashboard (Composio's Salesforce guide uses https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) as the app's Callback URL.

sources.t: Salesforce REST API: External Client Apps or Connected Apps
Salesforce CLI: create a connected app
How the AgentExchange security review works
Trailhead: package and distribute External Client Apps

unverified: Security review fee amount: older ISVforce guide versions listed $999 (and earlier $2,550), but the current docs page no longer states an amount and the old fee pages now 404.
Whether a 'Local' External Client App can authorize users from other orgs without packaging was not confirmed in fetched Salesforce docs.
Access token lifetime is not stated in the fetched pages.

name: Pipedrive
oneLiner: Private apps install via direct link, no review needed.

review.what: Pipedrive Marketplace app approval (only for public, listed apps)

cost.text: $0; no submission or listing fee is mentioned

limits.text: Private apps get no Marketplace listing page but can be shared with any Pipedrive company via an unlisted install link.

requirements.text: You need a developer sandbox account to access the Developer Hub.
Both private and public apps must use OAuth 2.0 with working install and uninstall flows.
Public apps need Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages and agreement to the Developer Partner Agreement.
Public app review needs a demo video, up-to-date test accounts, and 3-5 listing images.
The callback URL in requests must match the one entered when registering the app.

gotchas.text: The app type (private or public) cannot be changed later in Developer Hub.
Every user in a company installs the app separately; installs are per user.
Access tokens last 60 minutes; refresh tokens expire after 60 days unused, forcing a full reinstall.
Approved public apps are unlisted by default and must be published manually.
Don't click Install and Test in Pipedrive; start the connection from Composio and enter the company subdomain.
"App not found" usually means the client ID/secret don't match or the app isn't available to that user.

steps.t: Request a Pipedrive developer sandbox account
In Developer Hub, create a private app with a unique name and Composio's callback URL
Pick only the access scopes you need and copy the client ID and secret
Create a custom Pipedrive auth config in Composio with the client ID and secret
Connect from Composio, entering the Pipedrive company subdomain when asked

callbackNote: Add the redirect URI shown in Composio's dashboard (Composio's Pipedrive guide uses https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) as the app's Callback URL.

sources.t: Pipedrive: creating a proper app (public vs private)

unverified: Whether the developer sandbox account is free, and how long access takes, is not stated.
No install cap for private apps is stated, but no page explicitly says there is none.

name: Zendesk
oneLiner: Multi-customer apps need a Zendesk-issued global client.

review.what: Global OAuth client request through the Zendesk Marketplace portal

cost.text: No fee is mentioned for the global OAuth request

limits.text: Before approval: a local OAuth client's tokens only access the single Zendesk instance that created it.
Third-party apps may not use a customer's API token or the customer's own OAuth client, listed or not.

requirements.text: Apps distributed to multiple Zendesk customers must use global OAuth tokens.
Requests must come from a d3v- sponsored account; non-d3v- submissions aren't accepted.
Sponsored d3v- accounts are reserved for developers building Zendesk Marketplace apps.
The local client's unique identifier must start with zdg- and every field must be filled in.
Unlisted integrations must still create a Marketplace profile, register the organization and submit for review.
Global OAuth clients must support the refresh token flow from January 31, 2026.

gotchas.text: Save the client secret and identifier first; you lose the client admin page after conversion to global.
Zendesk may cap allowed scopes; requesting others returns 400 invalid_scope.
Scope changes after approval go through Zendesk Support, since only Marketplace Operations can edit global clients.
New global clients get 30-minute access tokens and 30-day refresh tokens by default.
A sponsored account is suspended if used to provide real customer support.
Integration apps must send custom headers identifying the integration, organization ID and Marketplace app ID.

steps.t: Start a Zendesk trial, rename the subdomain with a d3v- prefix and file the Sponsored Account Request Form
Create a local OAuth client with a zdg- identifier, all fields filled and Composio's redirect URL
Save the client ID and secret somewhere safe
Draft the scope list and justification for the global OAuth request
In the Marketplace portal, open Global OAuth and click Request new OAuth
After approval, create a custom Zendesk auth config in Composio with the saved credentials

callbackNote: Add the redirect URI shown in Composio's dashboard; Composio's Zendesk guide lists an older v1 URL (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add), so confirm against the dashboard.

name: Intercom
oneLiner: Only your team can install until review passes.

review.what: Intercom app review (required for both listed and unlisted public apps)

cost.text: $0; development workspaces are free and no review fee is mentioned

limits.text: Before approval the app is private and can only be used by you and your team.
Development workspaces cap at 20 users, can't send outbound email, and can't become production workspaces.

requirements.text: Public app developers must create a development workspace to build and publish the app.
OAuth redirect URLs must use HTTPS.
Review needs a video showing OAuth install, end-to-end functionality, and OAuth uninstall.
Requested scopes are checked against what the app does.
Unlisted apps must be installed from your own product or website.

gotchas.text: The authorization URL must use the regional host (US, EU or AU) matching the customer's workspace.
You may be asked to cut scopes and resubmit, which restarts the review.
OAuth is off until you tick "Use OAuth" on the app's Authentication page.
In EU and AU, development-workspace apps can't be installed into paid workspaces.

steps.t: Sign up for a free development workspace and create a new app in Developer Hub
Tick Use OAuth, add Composio's HTTPS redirect URL and select only the scopes you need
Copy the client ID and secret from Basic Information
Create a custom Intercom auth config in Composio with the client ID and secret
Record the install, functionality and uninstall video
Choose listed or unlisted and submit the app for review

callbackNote: Add the HTTPS redirect URI shown in Composio's dashboard on the app's Authentication page; the first redirect URL is the default.
unverified: Whether Intercom OAuth access tokens expire or use refresh tokens is not stated in the fetched pages.
Privacy policy and terms requirements sit in the developer terms, which were not fetched.
A search snippet said reviews take 7-14 days; the fetched page says up to seven business days.
